svg.text: ThermalNet: one frame, step by step
Every picture below is a real output of the trained model on one held-out thermal frame. Brighter = stronger.
The edge detector adds 8 extra pictures
Sobel and Laplacian are classic edge filters. Heat contrast is a pixel minus the average around it.
The 3 learned filters are tuned during training. Together with the frame, the model gets 9 pictures.
The backbone finds features, from fine detail to the big picture
Each stage halves the picture size
Early stages react to fine edges,
the last one to whole objects.
Every stage ends with attention that
Three grids say where objects are
In the pictures, bright = the cell is sure an object is here (object? × best class score).
The fine grid finds small objects, the coarse grid finds large ones.
many cells see the same person
keep the best box, drop others
that overlap it by 30% or more
is the hot shape a flat rectangle
Shapes and sizes come from the code; the model has 11.5 million parameters and no pretrained weights.
The person check applies to people only. It has 3 votes (shape, brightness, contrast); a box is rejected on 2 or more. The picture shows the shape vote.
